eligibility_reason: The paper reports original quantitative estimates of Americans' exposure to untrustworthy websites using web-browsing logs from October 8 to November 12, 2024. No text truncation is indicated.

estimates.measure: visited at least one untrustworthy website
estimates.misinfo_definition: Domain-level websites classified as untrustworthy because they publish false or misleading content or contradict the best available evidence from experts.
estimates.source_quote: In 2024, 16.5% (95% CI [13.7%, 19.4%]) of Americans visited at least one untrustworthy website, a significant decline from the 26.1% (95% CI [22.5%, 29.8%]) who did so in 2020 (H1, t = -5.567, p < 0.001, Cohen’s d = -0.236, one‑tailed) and the 44.3% (95% CI [40.8%, 47.7%]) who did so in 2016 (see Figure 1).

estimates.measure: visited at least one AI-generated untrustworthy website
estimates.misinfo_definition: AI-generated untrustworthy websites meeting NewsGuard UAINS criteria: substantial AI-produced content, publication without significant human oversight, presentation that could be mistaken for human-generated content, and no clear AI disclosure.
estimates.source_quote: We find that 6.5% (95% CI [4.6%, 8.5%]) of Americans visited at least one such site in 2024, significantly up from 2.6% (95% CI [1.3%, 4.0%]) in 2020 (H7, t = 4.37, p < 0.001, Cohen’s d = 0.187, one‑tailed).
